definitions.explanation: The process of drawing conclusions from evidence or known facts through logical thinking. Commonly associated with detective work and mystery fiction.

examples.japanese: {推理|すいり}{小説|しょうせつ}が{好|す}きだ。
{探偵|たんてい}は{鋭|するど}い{推理|すいり}で{犯人|はんにん}を{突|つ}き{止|と}めた。
examples.english: The detective identified the culprit through sharp deduction.

examples.japanese: {証拠|しょうこ}から{推理|すいり}すると、{犯行|はんこう}は{深夜|しんや}に{行|おこな}われたようだ。
examples.english: Reasoning from the evidence, it appears the crime was committed late at night.

notes: Composed of {推|すい} (conjecture, infer) + {理|り} (logic, reason). Most commonly encountered in {推理|すいり}{小説|しょうせつ} (mystery novel, detective fiction) and {推理|すいり}ドラマ (mystery drama/show). Can also be used as a verb: {推理|すいり}する (to reason, to deduce). Related words: {推測|すいそく} (conjecture, guess — less rigorous), {論理|ろんり} (logic — more abstract and academic).
